title: SLO Operationalization: Field Guide & Tactical Runbook (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, cross-functional field guide to move SLOs from definition into everyday operational practice for Redwood Inference services. It's a hands-on runbook for teams that need concrete steps, communication templates, and decision gates — not just principles.

Audience:
- Service owners and primary on-call engineers
- Product/PMs responsible for feature availability SLAs
- Platform & infra teams (autoscaling, routing, cache)
- Eng + SRE partners who will own instrumentation and alerts

High-level goal:
Reduce time-to-adoption for SLOs across product teams from weeks to days by providing ready-to-use artifacts: checks, alert thresholds, rollout gates, incident playbook snippets, and canary patterns.

Assumptions / Constraints:
- We expect telemetry (latency, error, throughput, success-fraction) to be available in our metrics backend for all routes by default. If not, priority onboarding is required (see onboarding checklist).
- Teams may opt-in to three SLO tiers (Platinum, Gold, Bronze) mapped to customer visibility and business impact.
- This guide is pragmatic: default thresholds are suggestions — teams must justify deviations in the SLO intake doc.

Quickstart checklist (3-steps to a usable SLO):
1) Define: pick objective (p99 latency / availability % / success-fraction), scope (route, model, region), and tier. Use the template in linked_confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234-slo-guidelines).
2) Instrument: add metrics exports and labels. Required tags: team, service, route, region, model_version. Reference SDK snippet in github.com/redwood-inference/slo-checks.
3) Rollout: start with canary: 2% traffic for 48h, 10% for 72h, then 50% for 48h; evaluate error budget spend. If healthy, full rollout.

SLO tiers (recommended defaults):
- Platinum: Availability 99.95% monthly; p99 latency < 250ms for critical routes. Requires dedicated alerting and 4h runbook.
- Gold: Availability 99.9% monthly; p99 latency < 500ms. Standard on-call + 1 business day target response.
- Bronze: Availability 99.5% monthly; p99 latency < 1s. Monitor-only with weekly reviews.

Rollout phases and guardrails:
- Phase 0 (Design): SLO intake doc filled; reviewers: SRE, infra, product.
- Phase 1 (Instrument-only): Metrics present, dashboards created, no user traffic pinned. 1 week observation.
- Phase 2 (Canary): Traffic split per quickstart. Automated rollback if canary consumes >50% of error budget in 24h.
- Phase 3 (Gradual): Increase traffic in steps with post-step signal check.
- Phase 4 (GA): Publicly announced and added to monthly reporting.

Incident playbook excerpts (short):
Trigger: error-rate or latency SLI breach + sustained for 5m
Immediate steps (T0–T15):
- T0: Pager -> primary on-call (tone: actionable context + last 5m graphs).
- T3: Run causal hypothesis checklist: recent deploys, traffic shift, model variant changes, infra events.
- T7: If coupling to infra discovered, engage platform pager.
- T10: Add incident channel (Slack) and named Incident Commander.

Containment (T15–T60):
- Apply quick mitigations: rollback, route to fallback model, increase replicas, enable cached responses.
- Use playbook snippets below for model fallback and KV cache warm-up.

Communication templates (for on-call):
- Incident open (first message): "INCIDENT: Service X experiencing elevated errors on route Y. Primary on-call: NAME. Current impact: Z% of requests failing (5m avg). First mitigation: rolling back model v3.2 -> v3.1. Update cadence: 15m."
- Postmortem header: "Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root Cause, Contributing Factors, What we did, Action Items (owners + ETA)"

Canary checklist (operator):
- Prepare traffic split rule (HA proxy / smart-router config).
- Apply instrumentation flag to route traffic to metric pipeline (verify labels present).
- Launch canary: 2% for 48h — monitor error budget, p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu load, and allocator OOMs.
- Pre-commit rollback policy: if any of the following happen, rollback immediately: error budget burn > 30% in 24h, p99 > threshold * 1.5, GPU mem pressure > 85% sustained 10m.

Metrics & dashboards to create (minimum):
- SLI timeseries: success_fraction (30d), p50/p95/p99 latency series, token generation time per inference.
- Error budget burn rate chart (1h, 6h, 24h windows).
- Resource cost per 1k tokens (to tie to Optimize suggestions).
- SLI by model_version to detect regressions quickly.

Owner matrix (proposal):
- Service Owner: SLO definition, product prioritization, customer comms.
- SRE: instrumentation review, alert tuning, incident playbook.
- Platform: scaling policies, routing, fallback support.
- Observability: dashboard templates, data retention policy.

Common gotchas and mitigation notes (observed from pilots):
- Missing labels: metrics aggregated at service-level hide route regressions. Mitigation: deny merge if service/route tags absent (CI check).
- Silent degradations: model hallucinations or correctness regressions are not captured by latency/error SLOs. Mitigation: add quality evals + synthetic checks to SLO catalog for high-risk routes.
- Cost blips during canary: autoscalers can overshoot. Mitigation: add budgeted scaling window during rollout.

Decision gates (must pass to proceed):
- Gate A (Instrument OK): dashboards green for 72h, signals stable, no regressions in model_version metric.
- Gate B (Canary OK): no SLO breach, error budget spend <10% of monthly in canary period, infra metrics within thresholds.
- Gate C (Business GO): product signs off on risk and communication plan.

Low-effort automation ideas (next sprint candidates):
- A CI check that validates required metric labels are present before merge.
- Auto-generated Slack incident channel + initial summary from latest graphs.
- A lightweight SLO intake form that wires a new SLO into dashboards and alert rules automatically.

Open questions / discussion items (for review meeting):
- Default lookback window for monthly availability SLOs: 28 days vs calendar month?
- How to incorporate model quality regressions into SLOs without inflating noise? (synthetic probes vs user feedback)
- Which team will own canary rollback automation across Dedicated and Private deployments?

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize canary thresholds and add to template repo (ETA 2026-08-22).
- Miguel: implement CI pre-merge metric label check (ETA 2026-09-05).
- Priya: draft product-facing SLO communications for Platinum tier (ETA 2026-08-29).

Appendix: Useful snippets and links
- Quick metric export example (prometheus/metrics client): see github.com/redwood-inference/slo-checks/examples/metrics-export.md
- Canary routing manifest template: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-routing/canary-template.yaml
- On-call escalation matrix: CONFLUENCE-2345-oncall-matrix

Notes to reviewers (rough):
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive: we expect teams to adapt thresholds but follow the pattern.
- Looking for feedback on the canary cadence and rollback thresholds; we've seen successes with longer small canaries for model-related rollouts.
- If you have a runbook snippet you want included, paste it in the comments and I'll fold it in.

---
Handy quick checklist (copy-paste for PR description):
- [ ] SLO intake completed and reviewed by SRE
- [ ] Metrics instrumented w/ required tags
- [ ] Dashboard created and linked in PR
- [ ] Canary plan attached to PR with rollback criteria
- [ ] Product comms drafted for user-facing impact

End of document.
